review: 1:1–1:3 חָזְקִי … תִּקְוָתִי … וּשְׁלוֹמִי — the Arabic إِنَّ قُوتِي … وَرَجَائِي … وَسَلَامِي is a threefold predicate chain resolved in the refrain; Hebrew keeps the same three nouns first and the answer last, which is how the stanza holds its suspense.
2:2 כִּסּוּיִי — the Arabic سِتْرِي is 'my covering'; כִּסּוּי is the biblical noun of covering (Exod 26:14), kept over the Modern Hebrew מִכְסֶה because the line needs the personal suffix.

4:2 יַרְאֵהוּ אַהֲבָתוֹ — the Arabic يَمْلَأُ الْقَلْبَ هَنَاءً وَيُرِيه / حُبَّهُ is 'fills the heart with bliss and shows it His love'; the Hebrew keeps the suffix chain (the heart is shown), rather than turning it into 'shows me'.

5:2–5:3 הָאוֹצָר … בַּמָּרוֹם — Matthew 6:20 (אוֹצָר בַּשָּׁמַיִם) with Col 3:1; the Arabic ذُخْرًا … فِي السَّمَاء / هُنَاكَ فِي الْعَلَاء is that treasure laid up above, and Hebrew keeps both the treasure and the place.
4:1–4:3 בִּשְׁקִיטָתִי וּבְבָדָד — the Arabic فِي سُكُونِي وَانْفِرَادِي is 'in my stillness and solitude'; בָּדָד is the biblical word for being alone (Ps 102:8), not the Modern Hebrew בְּדִידוּת.
